objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with itchy blisters in the axilla.

fragments.text: The patient, who recently moved to an assisted living facility, complains of itchy blisters that have developed in his axilla. He believes these blisters are due to a poor diet. Additionally, he mentions that since arriving at the facility, a nurse practitioner has started him on four new medications, adding to his already existing prescription regimen.
Belief that condition is due to poor diet
Details on specific past medical history are not provided, but patient has been on multiple medications prior to the new additions at the facility.
No details provided. Focus on patient's current living situation in an assisted living facility and recent medication changes.
Focused on skin symptoms; negative for fever, recent illnesses, or other systemic symptoms.

exam_leaves.text: Tense axillary bullae noted on the affected area.
The bullae do not rupture with light, gloved touch. Surrounding skin is warm and appears inflamed.

test_leaves.text: Linear C3 and IgG deposits along the basement membrane.
